scope: fresh current VM9 descriptor writer watch for the active callback trampoline
redaction: Only instruction offsets, descriptor fields, and log hashes are retained; request URLs, headers, device data, tokens, and raw traces remain local.

inputs.variation: same detail endpoint shape and frozen runtime setup; the book-id input was changed by one digit

active_path.semantics: ldp x1, x8, [x0]; mov x0, x8; br x1

cross_input_observation.interpretation: The active descriptor writer is stable across this two-input probe, while later native/allocator execution diverges. This writer is therefore a real boundary fact but not the missing input parameterization by itself.

established: The active current path reaches the +0x2584ac descriptor trampoline; the older +0x2887f0 candidate is not needed for this path.
Descriptor field writes are directly observed before the trampoline and originate from the VM store at +0x171268.
The trampoline's field8 is the object passed as x0 to the branch target; it is not proof of the previously observed packed entry-x8 composition.
conclusion.remaining_unknown: The callback-object writer/composition for the packed entry x8 pair (0x440132f775952fa9 / 0x1dc9821c75952fa9) is still uncaptured. Allocator refill and host handoff state are also not independently initialized.
conclusion.use_as_evidence: Use this record to place the active descriptor writer at the VM/native boundary and to reject the claim that the old +0x2887f0 helper is the current call site. It does not justify a pure-Python Medusa implementation or a no-JVM Rust signer.

limitations: Both runs are local Unidbg probes; neither produced a new server request.
The probe run ended in an existing native emulation fetch/read fault after the descriptor observation; the observation itself occurred before that fault.
No fresh-input body or independent allocator implementation was produced.
